security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives from Markdown code spans, documentation examples, and validation error messages. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or unauthorized command execution was found. One implementation weakness remains: the initializer uses the provided skill name as a path component without validation.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated skill names can affect where generated files are created.
remediation.suggestion: Reject names containing slashes, parent-directory segments, leading dots, or characters outside lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens before creating directories.

remediation.issue: The initializer trusts the requested output path without a containment check.
remediation.suggestion: After resolving the final skill directory, verify it remains inside the intended skills base directory before writing files.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Skill Name Can Escape Target Directory
semantic_findings.description: The initializer takes skill_name from argv and appends it directly to the requested output path. A name containing path separators or parent-directory segments could create files outside the intended skills directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly combines Path(path).resolve() with the raw skill_name argument and performs directory creation later. Legitimate use is expected, but malformed names are not rejected in this script.

content.user_title: Create Agent Skills with Guided Structure
content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable guidance for building reliable AI skills. This skill explains structure, scaffolding, validation, and iteration for skill packages.
actual_capabilities: Explains the required SKILL.md frontmatter and body structure.
Guides users through planning workflows, references, scripts, and assets.
Provides an initializer script that creates a starter skill package.
Provides a validator script for basic frontmatter and naming checks.
Describes iteration steps for improving an existing skill after use.
limitations: Does not publish skills to a marketplace or remote registry.
Does not verify that generated scripts are secure or correct.
Does not include advanced schema validation for every skill asset.
Requires the user to supply accurate examples and domain context.

use_cases.title: Create a first skill
use_cases.description: Plan a new skill, choose its structure, and scaffold the initial package.

use_cases.title: Standardize team skills
use_cases.description: Apply common naming, frontmatter, resource, and validation practices across multiple skills.

use_cases.title: Improve an existing skill
use_cases.description: Review weak instructions, move long content into references, and validate the updated package.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a simple skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a skill for a repeatable task. Ask for the minimum context, then propose the skill structure.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold a skill package
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new skill named my-workflow-helper in my skills directory. Include only the resources that are needed.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an existing skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this existing skill for clarity, progressive disclosure, and unnecessary files. Update it while preserving its purpose.

prompt_templates.title: Design a complex skill system
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a skill for a multi-step workflow with scripts, references, validation steps, and realistic forward-test prompts.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for monthly finance reporting.
output_examples.output: A planned skill outline with trigger description, workflow sections, suggested reference files, validation steps, and next actions.
A concise validation result that identifies frontmatter, naming, and description issues with suggested fixes.
A slimmer main instruction file plus guidance on which detailed material should move into references.

best_practices: Start from concrete user tasks before choosing scripts, references, or assets.
Keep SKILL.md focused and move detailed reference material into separate files.
Run validation after edits and test scripts that the skill introduces.
anti_patterns: Creating extra documentation files that do not support runtime skill use.
Putting every domain detail into SKILL.md instead of using references.
Adding scripts or assets before proving that repeated use needs them.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create AI skill packages with clear instructions, optional resources, and validation steps.

faq.question: Can it update an existing skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for revising instructions, resources, and validation practices.

faq.question: Does it require scripts in every skill?
faq.answer: No. Scripts are recommended only when repeated or fragile work needs deterministic execution.

faq.question: Does it create marketplace metadata?
faq.answer: No. The included workflow focuses on local skill structure and basic validation.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What should users provide first?
faq.answer: Users should provide the task, target workflow, expected triggers, and any domain examples.
